idiom_name: hand-rolled seen-set (hsearch table) or an SQLite `INSERT OR IGNORE` inbox
implementation_notes: C ships no seen-set container: the classic structure is written by hand. In-process, POSIX hcreate/hsearch (man 3 hsearch) gives a hash table keyed by the message id, but it is process-local, non-reentrant and not thread-safe, so it only fits single-threaded receivers and loses everything on restart. The realistic durable realization is an SQLite inbox: `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO seen(id, at) VALUES(?1, ?2)` followed by sqlite3_changes() - one changed row means this delivery won the claim, zero means a duplicate. Keep the claim and the business write in one SQLite transaction and prune rows older than the broker's redelivery window with a periodic DELETE. Where a framework-level broker client exists, prefer its deduplication hooks over this hand-rolled store.
pitfalls: hcreate/hsearch tables are process-local and not thread-safe; a multi-threaded or multi-process receiver silently loses its protection.
Claim and effects must share one SQLite transaction: committing the claim before the effects loses the message, committing the effects first duplicates it.
Never pruning the seen table (or pruning too early) breaks the guarantee in opposite ways: unbounded growth versus reopened duplicates.
